Field notes on quiet mornings

By Sam Example

For four weeks I kept a notebook by the door and wrote one line every morning before looking at a screen. The rule was simple: no phone until the line was written. Most days the line was about the weather, the light or the noise from the street.

By the second week the notebook had become the first thing I reached for. I started to notice that the mornings I wrote anything at all were calmer than the mornings I skipped it, even when the line itself was dull.

What I counted

I counted how long it took before I first unlocked the phone. The numbers are rough, written down by hand, but the trend is clear enough to share.

WeekMedian minutesDays skipped
143
2111
3180
4221

The small script

To keep myself honest I wrote a tiny script that prints how many lines the notebook file has, so I could not pretend I had written more than I had.

wc -l notebook.txt

It is not clever, but it was enough.
